full_judgment:
8. Mr Nurullah next submits that the respondent being a Teacher of the University should have preferred an appeal before the Chancellor for redress of his grievance which is an equally efficacious remedy provided by law as per provisions contemplated in Article 52 of the Dhaka University Order, 1973, as has been upheld in the case of the Controller of Examinations vs Mohammad Mohiuddin, (1992) 12 BLD (AD) 309. 

 9. In the afore cited case this Division held that if the High Court Division is satisfied by exercising its discretion judicially that the alternative remedy provided in a particular case is not adequate and effective, then, such discretion can hardly be interfered with. But in the cited case the High Court Division did not apply properly their mind as to the law and facts of the case and it misconceived the whole matter as to the provisions of Article 52 wrongly holding that the Chancellor's decision on the appeal is dependent upon the opinion of the University authority who had passed the impugned order. As such the discretion exercised by the High Court Division in the cited case was not found to be a discretion exercised judicially. 

 10. In the present case we find that in their affidavit-in-opposition the respondent-petitioners referred to the provisions of alternative remedy in Paragraph 17 thereof. But throughout the lengthy impugned judgment of the High Court Division it does not appear that this basic preliminary point of maintainability was agitated at all. Although it is contended in paragraph 6 of the leave petition that Article 52 of the Dhaka University Order, 1973 was categorically canvassed before the High Court Division we have no manner of knowing how it was done, casually or otherwise, when the impugned judgment is absolutely silent about it and no reference has been made to the arguments and counter-arguments made by the parties with regard to the maintainability of the writ petition. Therefore discretion once exercised in such circumstances without any opposition will not be interfered with simply on the ground of availability of alternative efficacious remedy especially when the decision sought to be appealed from does not suffer from any infirmity of law.
